data.claim: complete() strips all gate blockers for a settled umbrella so its gates stay silent
data.falsifier: an umbrella completed via last child has gate events of its own
data.mechanism: complete.py filters v.blockers to open-bug only
data.probe_output: 1 failed, 2 passed: AssertionError the umbrella completed with its gates silent
data.question: Does umbrella auto-complete leave gates silent?

evidence.note: brief rules/decisions read; none touches umbrella gates; no weakening for ordinary items
umbrella.roll_up records skipped rolled-up outcomes before verdict; tests/test_umbrella_gates.py + umbrella_completes + subtasks: 31 passed

chunk_findings.detail: The new allowlist `KEPT = (OPEN_BUG_BLOCKER, "gate(s) never run", "awaiting a person")` is a prefix whitelist applied to *all* of the verdict's blockers, so every blocker whose text does not begin with one of those three strings is silently deleted for an umbrella, even though the old code only had to drop the diff-related blockers and the comment claims "an open bug or a silent gate holds it". Concretely: an umbrella's gate that already carries a non-silent outcome — e.g. someone recorded `ddflow gate record <umbrella> unit_tests failed`, or a gate ended `failed` after being run — is *not* in `roll_up`'s `silent` set, so it keeps its failed outcome, and `CM.verdict` reports a blocker for it whose text ("...failed..." / "...did not pass...") matches none of the three prefixes; the comprehension empties `v.blockers` and the umbrella reaches done with a failed gate, which is precisely the class of hole the change claims to close, reached through a failed rather than a silent gate. The same filter also drops any non-enumerated reason to hold an umbrella — e.g. a "sub-task(s) still open" or "missing evidence" blocker: `roll_up` is invoked unconditionally for any item with children, it stamps the still-silent gates as `skipped, rolled up from the sub-tasks: <ids>` naming the children (`umbrella.py` `evidence={"rolled_up_from": ...}`), and because those stamped outcomes are then excluded from `silent` and persisted in the append-only log ("a gate that already holds an outcome keeps it"), the umbrella can complete while naming children that are not finished. The described regression test cannot catch any of this: it only asserts that every gate of the umbrella has an outcome plus child-naming evidence, which is exactly what `roll_up` writes, never that a non-silent *failing* gate or a non-enumerated blocker still stops the umbrella.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py (the `v.blockers = [b for b in v.blockers if b.startswith(UM.KEPT)]` filter)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py (the `v.blockers = [b for b in v.blockers if b.startswith(UM.KEPT)]` filter)

chunk_findings.detail: The intent's fix has two halves: (a) auto-record the umbrella's gates on close, and (b) remove the gate-guard exemption for umbrella items. The test meant to pin half (b) uses `P.T` with **no sub-tasks**. The exemption applied to umbrella items (items with children); a childless item was never exempt, so the guard already refused it *before* the fix. I verified by reasoning over the code paths: with the unfixed code (exemption still present) this test passes exactly as written, because `is_umbrella(P.T)` is false and the exemption is never consulted. Consequence: an implementation that keeps the exemption and only adds the rollup passes the whole suite, so the suite does not verify the required removal. The uncovered scenario is a real one: completing an umbrella **directly** (e.g. `complete P.T` while `P.T.a`/`P.T.b` are still open) never runs the cascade rollup, so its gates stay silent; with the old exemption retained, the guard would let it complete with zero outcomes — precisely the reported bug class. No test in this file exercises that path, and `test_an_ordinary_item...`'s name implies it does.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_umbrella_gates.py:58 (`test_an_ordinary_item_with_silent_gates_is_still_refused`)

chunk_findings.detail:
`code, out, err = run_cli(repo, "gate", "status", "P.T")` discards the exit code and asserts only `"never run" not in out + err`. If `gate status` were broken for an umbrella (non-zero exit, no status output at all), `out + err` would contain no "never run" and this assertion passes vacuously — the completeness claim ("never silent" for *every* gate) then rests only on the `assert evs`/per-event checks, which never compare the recorded gates against the pipeline's gate set. The test would still pass if the fix recorded only a proper subset of the umbrella's gates (e.g. only one gate), as long as every event it did emit looked right. Asserting `code == OK` and comparing the set of gates in `gate status` against the recorded events would close that hole.

Guidance check: D-rules-format (TOML/frontmatter) and D-rules-hierarchy raise no issue with this change; a regression test is present, so the "must have regression test" constraint is not violated.

titles: ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py (the `v.blockers = [b for b in v.blockers if b.startswith(UM.KEPT)]` filter)

chunk_findings.detail: `UM.verdict` runs `roll_up` unconditionally, *before* any blocker/close decision, and `complete.py` computes the verdict on every invocation (the non-closing path too — the `if closing:` filter only runs afterwards). The intent states the outcome must be recorded "when the umbrella closes", but here writing happens on any verdict computation, including ones that are then refused. Concrete case: an umbrella `P.T` filed to fix a bug that is still open — run `ddflow complete P.T`; `roll_up` appends a `skipped` record with `reason="rolled up from the sub-tasks: c1, c2"` and `evidence={"rolled_up_from": [...]}` for every silent gate, then `blockers()` keeps `OPEN_BUG_BLOCKER` and the command aborts. `ddflow gate status P.T` now reports rolled-up outcomes that were never earned (and the evidence names children that may not even be complete, and goes stale if a child is added later). Recording should be deferred to the point where the umbrella actually closes, or rolled back when the completion is refused.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/umbrella.py `roll_up` (called from ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py:104)

chunk_findings.detail: Still holds: the implementation half of this change removes the umbrella exemption by no longer shedding the "gate(s) … never run" blocker (`SHED` in umbrella.py deliberately omits it), but the test that is supposed to pin that half uses `P.T` with no sub-tasks. `umbrella` is falsy for a childless item, so the old code never applied the exemption to it and the guard already refused it before the fix; the test therefore passes identically on the unfixed code and proves nothing about the exemption. The only way to observe the exemption removal is an umbrella for which `roll_up` leaves a gate silent (`G.record` raising `ValueError`, e.g. a non-skippable/human gate) and then asserting the guard still refuses — nothing in this change does that.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_umbrella_gates.py:58 `test_an_ordinary_item_with_silent_gates_is_still_refused`

chunk_findings.detail: Still holds: `code, out, err = run_cli(repo, "gate", "status", "P.T")` discards the exit code and asserts only `"never run" not in out + err`. If `gate status` returned nothing (or crashed with an empty status payload), the assertion would pass vacuously. The completeness claim ("never silent" *for every* gate) is never checked against the pipeline's gate set — the test only checks the events it already knows about, so a regression that stopped recording some gate would slip through.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_umbrella_gates.py:46 `test_closing_the_last_child_gives_every_umbrella_gate_an_outcome`

chunk_findings.detail: This test still cannot fail if half (b) of the fix is not done. The exemption that B8b2dafcbf3 added, and that this item claims to remove, applied to umbrella items — items with sub-tasks (the intent says "an item with sub-tasks ... the gate guard of B8b2dafcbf3 had to exempt such items"). The test drives `P.T` created with `task add` and *no* `split`, so `P.T` never has children and was never covered by the exemption; the guard already refused it before the fix. Take the fixed tree and reinstate the exemption (`if is_umbrella(item): skip the "every gate has an outcome" check`): test_closing_the_last_child... still passes (the rollup writes the outcomes before the guard runs), test_an_outcome_the_umbrella_already_has_is_kept still passes, test_a_settled_umbrella_completed_directly_gets_rolled_up_gates still passes (the rollup pre-empts the guard), and test_a_failed_umbrella_gate_still_holds_the_umbrella still passes, because a *failed* gate is a present outcome, not a "never run" one, so the exemption for the "never run" rule never suppresses that blocker. No test in the file distinguishes presence from absence of the umbrella exemption for an item that actually has children.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_umbrella_gates.py:57 (`test_an_ordinary_item_with_silent_gates_is_still_refused`)

chunk_findings.detail: The intent requires that *every gate in the pipeline* of the umbrella carries an outcome, but this test only asserts that the events that happen to exist have the right shape (`assert evs`, then per-event `kind`/reason/evidence). It never compares the recorded gate set against the pipeline's gate set, and the only set-equality assertion in the file is in test_a_settled_umbrella_completed_directly_gets_rolled_up_gates, which merely checks `>= {"implement", "merge", "unit_tests"}`. The file itself shows a gate outside that triple: `research` is a valid gate for `P.T` (test_an_outcome_the_umbrella_already_has_is_kept line 50 records `gate skip P.T research` and asserts success). Therefore a fix that rolls up only the gates it knows about and leaves `research` silent on the last-child path passes both tests, even though that is exactly the "silence is not a pass" condition this bug is about.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_umbrella_gates.py:41 (`test_closing_the_last_child_gives_every_umbrella_gate_an_outcome`)

chunk_findings.detail: `UM.verdict` writes the rolled-up gate outcomes *inside the verdict computation*, before `complete.py` has looked at `v.blockers` and decided whether the umbrella may close. Every refused completion therefore leaves permanent, never-undone `skipped` gate events on the record. Concrete input: umbrella `P` (children `A`,`B`, both done) that was filed to fix an open bug, so `CM.verdict` returns `OPEN_BUG_BLOCKER` — or whose pipeline contains a checkpoint gate that yields "awaiting a person". Running `ddflow complete P` (or the auto-close triggered by `B` finishing) is refused, yet `roll_up` has already recorded `skipped`, reason "rolled up from the sub-tasks: A, B", evidence `{"rolled_up_from": ["A","B"]}` for every gate, so `ddflow gate status P` afterwards shows an outcome for each gate of an item that never closed, with evidence asserting a roll-up that was never applied to a close. The intent says to "record that outcome when the umbrella closes"; recording at verdict time (a judgement call that is also reached on aborted attempts) makes the operation non-idempotent and produces skipped-gate records for umbrellas that remain open — and, because the gates are then no longer silent, the item can no longer be held on those gate outcomes if the underlying situation later changes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/umbrella.py (verdict → roll_up)

chunk_findings.detail: This finding still holds — nothing in the change answers it. The intent's fix has two halves: (a) `roll_up` auto-records the umbrella's gates, and (b) the gate-guard exemption for umbrella items is removed. The test that is supposed to pin (b) uses `P.T` with no sub-tasks, and a childless item was never covered by the umbrella exemption, so the guard already refused it before the fix: the test passes on the unfixed code and cannot fail as a regression probe for half (b). Removing the exemption (which is not visible in this part of the diff) does not make the test meaningful; only giving the test an item *with* children would.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_umbrella_gates.py:58 (test_an_ordinary_item_with_silent_gates_is_still_refused)

chunk_findings.detail: This finding still holds — nothing in the change answers it. `code, out, err = run_cli(repo, "gate", "status", "P.T")` discards the exit code and asserts only `"never run" not in out + err`, so if `gate status` exits non-zero with no output for an umbrella, the assertion passes vacuously. The completeness claim ("never silent" for *every* gate) then rests only on `assert evs` / per-event checks, which never compare the recorded gates against the pipeline's gate set, so a gate that `roll_up` silently failed to record (the `except ValueError: continue` path) would not be caught by this test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_umbrella_gates.py:46 (test_closing_the_last_child_gives_every_umbrella_gate_an_outcome)

chunk_findings.detail: The intent's fix has two halves: (a) auto-record an umbrella's gates on close, and (b) remove the gate-guard exemption for umbrella items. This test is the one named for half (b), but it builds `P.T` with `task add "P.T" ... --globs a.py` and no children, so `P.T` is not an umbrella. The exemption applied only to items that have children, so a childless item was already refused by the guard *before* the fix. Concretely, run this test with the exemption still in place for umbrellas: `run_cli(repo, "complete", "P.T")` fails with a "never run" message exactly as asserted, and `_umbrella_gate_events(repo)` is empty because the failed completion records nothing — every assertion in the test is satisfied. The test therefore gives no regression signal for the removal it is supposed to pin, and half (b) of the change is left unpinned by the file as written. The fix (part 2) does not answer the earlier report: the item under test is still created without sub-tasks.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_umbrella_gates.py:58 (`test_an_ordinary_item_with_silent_gates_is_still_refused`)
